record.paper_title: Boundary and Defect CFT: Open Problems and Applications
record.original_question: Can standard two-dimensional conformal-field-theory constructions, such as orbifolding and perturbation theory, be reproduced or generalized on quasi Riemann surfaces so as to generate new theories of higher-dimensional defects?

evidence.quote: It should be possible to imitate on the quasi Riemann surfaces the usual constructions of 2d cft such as orbifolding and perturbation theory.

artifact.category_tag: Higher-dimensional defect CFT on quasi Riemann surfaces
artifact.self_contained_problem:
A quasi Riemann surface is a higher-dimensional generalization of a Riemann surface designed to support a notion of conformal field theory whose "fields" are extended (higher-dimensional) defect operators rather than point operators. On a quasi Riemann surface one expects an analogue of the algebra of local operators, operator product expansion, and partition/correlation functions, with the role of points played by submanifolds (defects).

Develop, on quasi Riemann surfaces, analogues of the standard two-dimensional conformal field theory constructions—specifically:

(a) Orbifolding: Given a quasi Riemann surface X equipped with the action of a (finite) symmetry group G of the underlying CFT-like structure, construct an "orbifold" CFT on X/G by (i) restricting to G-invariant defect operators, (ii) introducing twisted defect sectors labelled by conjugacy classes of G, and (iii) defining modular-invariant (or suitably consistent) partition and correlation functions summing over these sectors.

(b) Perturbation theory: Given a CFT-like structure on a quasi Riemann surface X together with a marginal or nearly marginal higher-dimensional defect operator O, define and compute order-by-order deformations of the correlation functions of the theory by O, in analogy with conformal perturbation theory in two dimensions.

The problem is to determine whether such constructions can be carried out rigorously on quasi Riemann surfaces, and to use them to produce new, nontrivial theories of higher-dimensional defects (i.e., new examples of defect CFTs in dimension greater than two), establishing their basic consistency properties (e.g., associativity of the defect OPE, invariance under the relevant symmetry group of the quasi Riemann surface, and finiteness of the perturbative expansion).
artifact.status_search_result: No published constructions implementing orbifolding or perturbation theory on quasi Riemann surfaces to produce new higher-dimensional defect CFTs were located. The problem is posed as a direction for future work and appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: QFT with defects in nLab
status_evidence.snippet: Overview of defect QFT, with focus on 2d rational CFT (FRS theorem) and no construction on quasi Riemann surfaces.
status_evidence.claim: Standard defect-CFT literature treats 2d cases; no analogue on quasi Riemann surfaces is reported.

status_evidence.title: C=1 conformal field theories on Riemann surfaces
status_evidence.snippet: Orbifold CFT constructions on ordinary Riemann surfaces.
status_evidence.claim: Orbifold/perturbation constructions are well-developed on classical Riemann surfaces but not on quasi Riemann surfaces.
